items.text: The system shall, before each Autopilot activation, require the driver to acknowledge that they remain responsible for monitoring the road and shall keep that responsibility visible while Autopilot is engaged.
items.context: Obstacle: The driver looks away from the road or stops actively monitoring because Autopilot appears to be handling the drive, leaving hazards unnoticed and no timely intervention. | Premise: The driver understands that Level 2 assistance does not take responsibility for monitoring and will remain attentive even when the system is operating.

items.text: The system shall treat an object in the vehicle’s projected path that is detected but cannot be confidently classified as a potential hazard, and shall warn the driver or initiate braking when its estimated path presents a collision risk.
items.context: Obstacle: Vision processing misclassifies or suppresses an uncertain or unusual object ahead, such as a stationary road hazard or work-zone object, so it is not detected in time for a safe response. | Premise: Relevant objects in the vehicle’s path will be recognized reliably, including objects that do not look like ordinary vehicles.

items.text: When lane-marking confidence is below the validated operating threshold or lane cues conflict, Autosteer shall stop issuing lane-following steering commands and alert the driver.
items.context: Obstacle: At an interchange or HOV-lane split, Autosteer follows ambiguous, degraded, or conflicting lane markings or the path of another vehicle and steers out of the intended lane. | Premise: Lane markings and the vehicle ahead consistently indicate the correct lane to follow.

items.text: The system shall initiate automatic emergency braking, when a collision threat is detected, no later than the point at which the remaining distance equals the validated stopping distance for the vehicle’s speed and braking capability.
items.context: Obstacle: Automatic emergency braking does not begin early enough because a hazard is detected late, its motion is estimated inaccurately, or the system’s intervention threshold is reached only when little stopping distance remains. | Premise: Any collision threat that requires emergency braking will be recognized with enough time and certainty for braking to prevent or reduce the impact.

items.text: TACC shall not accelerate toward the set speed when it has no tracked lead vehicle unless the sensed forward path is confirmed clear; if path occupancy is uncertain, it shall withhold acceleration and alert the driver.
items.context: Obstacle: TACC concludes that no vehicle is ahead when a vehicle or other hazard is present but not tracked, and returns to the driver’s set speed toward it. | Premise: If TACC has no tracked lead vehicle, the road ahead is clear for acceleration to the set speed.

items.text: When a lead vehicle changes lanes or another vehicle cuts in, TACC shall track the replacement lead vehicle before the selected following gap is breached or, if it cannot do so, reduce speed and alert the driver.
items.context: Obstacle: A lead vehicle changes lanes or is cut off, and TACC fails to reacquire the relevant vehicle or adjust promptly, so the chosen following gap is not maintained. | Premise: The vehicle being followed remains the relevant lead vehicle, or TACC will promptly identify a replacement when traffic changes.

items.text: The system shall not treat steering torque alone as confirmation that the driver is ready to take control; following a driver-monitoring prompt, it shall require a deliberate driver response before continuing to rely on driver availability.
items.context: Obstacle: Steering torque is treated as evidence that the driver’s hands are on the wheel even when the driver is not actually holding it or is not ready to steer. | Premise: Measured steering torque reliably indicates both physical hand contact and the driver’s ability to take control.

items.text: The system shall issue a visual and audible driver-monitoring alert when the configured no-steering-input interval expires, and shall escalate the alert before that interval exceeds the maximum validated time for driver intervention.
items.context: Obstacle: The visual and audible alerts occur only after the driver has been inattentive long enough that a developing hazard leaves insufficient time to respond. | Premise: A delay before alerting is safe because the driver will notice hazards and intervene before the alert is needed.

items.text: When occlusion or sensing conditions prevent reliable observation of a relevant part of the forward path, the system shall indicate reduced sensing capability and inhibit any assistance function that would otherwise rely on that unobserved area.
items.context: Obstacle: The sensors fail to provide usable information about a relevant part of the surroundings because an object is occluded or the sensing conditions prevent reliable observation. | Premise: The forward-facing sensors provide adequate information about every hazard relevant to the vehicle’s path.

items.text: Road-work deployments shall separate workers and equipment from live travel lanes or provide conspicuous advance warning at a distance sufficient for approaching traffic to stop safely.
items.context: Obstacle: Road work places workers or equipment unexpectedly in or near a live travel lane, creating a hazard that drivers and assistance functions may not anticipate. | Premise: Road work will remain separated from moving traffic or will be clearly marked and detectable in time.

System description:
# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.

stages.prompt:
You are a safety analyst doing obstacle analysis on a goal model.

An obstacle is a condition that prevents a goal from being satisfied.
For EACH goal below, propose obstacles. Use these guide words to search:
- omission: the system or an actor does not do something it should
- commission: it does something it should not
- too early / too late: it acts at the wrong time

Also check these obstacle types:
- non-information: an actor never gets information it needs
- wrong belief: an actor assumes something about the world that can be false
- inaccuracy: information is imprecise, unstable or out of date
- unavailability: a needed agent or resource is missing or switched off

Do not only think about sensor or hardware faults. Also think about what people and other road users
actually do (for example a pedestrian in an unexpected place, an operator who looks away or relies too
much on the system), how the system classifies and tracks objects, and what it does with uncertain
detections (for example ignoring or suppressing them).

For every obstacle, name the hidden premise it violates: the assumption that someone
thought was too obvious to write down.

Return at most 10 obstacles in total, ranked from most to least important for safety.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"obstacles": [{"id": "o1", "goal_id": "g1", "guide_word": "omission",
                "text": "...", "violated_premise": "..."}]}

requirements.text: The system shall, before each Autopilot activation, require the driver to acknowledge that they remain responsible for monitoring the road and shall keep that responsibility visible while Autopilot is engaged.

The system shall treat an object in the vehicle’s projected path that is detected but cannot be confidently classified as a potential hazard, and shall warn the driver or initiate braking when its estimated path presents a collision risk.
When lane-marking confidence is below the validated operating threshold or lane cues conflict, Autosteer shall stop issuing lane-following steering commands and alert the driver.

The system shall initiate automatic emergency braking, when a collision threat is detected, no later than the point at which the remaining distance equals the validated stopping distance for the vehicle’s speed and braking capability.

TACC shall not accelerate toward the set speed when it has no tracked lead vehicle unless the sensed forward path is confirmed clear; if path occupancy is uncertain, it shall withhold acceleration and alert the driver.

When a lead vehicle changes lanes or another vehicle cuts in, TACC shall track the replacement lead vehicle before the selected following gap is breached or, if it cannot do so, reduce speed and alert the driver.

The system shall not treat steering torque alone as confirmation that the driver is ready to take control; following a driver-monitoring prompt, it shall require a deliberate driver response before continuing to rely on driver availability.

The system shall issue a visual and audible driver-monitoring alert when the configured no-steering-input interval expires, and shall escalate the alert before that interval exceeds the maximum validated time for driver intervention.

When occlusion or sensing conditions prevent reliable observation of a relevant part of the forward path, the system shall indicate reduced sensing capability and inhibit any assistance function that would otherwise rely on that unobserved area.
Road-work deployments shall separate workers and equipment from live travel lanes or provide conspicuous advance warning at a distance sufficient for approaching traffic to stop safely.
